_about: DC-10-30 (passenger; the DC-10-10 and -40 share its fuselage and fin), from Boeing's copy of McDonnell Douglas's DC/MD-10 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (DAC-67803A, reprinted January 1991, Revision A April 2004; boeing.com's airport planning page, DC10.pdf, 2023), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions, Model DC-10 Series 30 and 30CF (Lower Galley) (page index 13): side, plan and front views on one sheet, a 1-bit scan on graph paper. Pixels of layers.py --mode image rasters, --unrotate --rotate 180, line centres: side at scale 4 (clip 120,300,505,434), plan at 4.047 with --xscale 0.9884 (clip 120,382,505,722; drawn 1.2% narrow across by its own 6.02 m dimension), front at 4 (clip 137,132,492,262; its circle drawn 2% small, so crownTop is the circle's middle less the printed radius). Scaled by the printed 51.97 m (170 ft 6 in) from the nose to the tail cone (23, 1409 px, where that dimension's extension line meets the tail cone: 26.67 px a meter); the overall 55.35 m reaches the tail engine's exhaust. The MD-11's placed points (md11/) moved by plug.py (3.0 m out at 15 m, 3.68 m at 40 m), then the fuselage's tail, fin, tail engine, wing engine, wing and tailplane placed here. Tail engine as the MD-11's (`tailEngine`, straight duct; strut 1160-1420 px). Windows drawn: each one's middle listed (`windows.x`), the doors' own windows and the cockpit's glass left out; four Type A doors as drawn on the left (both sides). The 30CF's main-deck cargo door (dashed) and the lower-deck cargo doors left out. Cockpit panes: the MD-11's. Rebuild: layers.py per view, snap.py, features.py, build.py dc10/recipe.json W, smooth.py, windshield.py. The plan draws the tailplane 3.2% short of the printed 21.69 m while the front view draws it within 0.2%: `stabilizerSpan: printed`.

sources.title: Boeing (McDonnell Douglas Corporation, Douglas Aircraft Company), DC/MD-10 Airplane Characteristics for Airport Planning (DAC-67803A, reprinted January 1991, Revision A April 2004), 2.2 General Airplane Dimensions: Model DC-10 Series 30 and 30CF (Lower Galley)
sources.note: Dimensions and outlines read off the DC-10-30 sheet's side, plan and front views (tools/trace/dc10/), starting from the MD-11's placed points moved by plug.py; the figures are the aircraft's measurements, not a copy of the drawing. The sheet is a 1-bit scan on graph paper (about 27.5 px a meter, so outlines are good to about 5 cm). Scaled by the printed 51.97 m (170 ft 6 in) from the nose to the tail cone. The plan is drawn 1.2% narrow across (by its own 6.02 m width dimension), rendered to the side's scale; the front view's fuselage circle is drawn 2% small (tied to the side by its middle). Its plan draws the tailplane 3.2% short of the printed 21.69 m (the front view within 0.2%), so the tailplane is widened to the printed span outboard of its root. Three CF6-50 nacelles: two under the wing and the third through the fin's base on a short strut, the fin's leading edge standing on its top and a fairing over its nozzle (engines[0], mount tail, a straight duct, as the MD-11's). The sheet draws the cabin windows, four doors a side (the left side's drawn; the DC-10's are the same both sides) and, dashed, the 30CF's main-deck cargo door, left out here (a passenger shape); the lower-deck cargo doors aren't placed. Cockpit panes: the MD-11's (the same nose). One shape for the DC-10-10, -30 and -40 passenger airframes: the -30 and -40 have the -10's fuselage and fin, but their wing spans 50.39 m against the -10's 47.35 m (the -10 here is 1.5 m too wide each side); the -30 and -40 have a third main gear leg on the centerline (not modeled: shapes have no gear), and the -40's nacelles are the JT9D-20's, not the CF6-50's drawn here. Confidence medium: a scan.

windows.note: Each window's place along the body measured on the DC-10-30 sheet's side view (2.2), which draws them as small closed outlines: 60 on the left side between doors 1 and 4 (one under the 30CF cargo door's dashed outline placed on the pitch), the doors' own windows left out; their height and width the drawing's (line centres).
